faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees, set at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are higher minimums for specific industries and occupations, set by the Fair Work Commission. Most employees are covered by an award, so their minimum pay is higher than the National Minimum Wage. You can find your award rate using the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage base rate is $26.44 per hour; with casual loading it becomes $33.05 per hour. Our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator applies it for you.

faqs.q: Is super included in my hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your hourly rate. Your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, separate from your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer pays an extra $7,200 into super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding your hourly rate in Australia

If you’re paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. In Australia, the calculation is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. But there are important Australian rules to understand, including the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation paid on top. This guide explains each step and shows how your pay compares to the average American salary.

### The National Minimum Wage and award rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services (SCHADS Award has specific pay rates that may be higher. Always check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual loading: 25% on top

Casual employees receive an extra 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. Our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the calculator applies it for you. This loading is not a penalty rate; it’s a standard entitlement for casuals.

### Superannuation paid on top

Superannuation is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top by your employer. It’s not deducted from your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer pays $7,200 into super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is separate from your pay. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

## Converting hourly to annual: the 38-hour week

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours. Multiply: hourly × 38 × 52 = annual gross. For a full-time adult on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross = $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.40. If casual, add 25% loading: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,317.20 annual gross. Fortnightly: weekly × 2. For the National Minimum Wage: $1,009.40 per week, fortnight = $2,018.80. The [hourly conversion](/blog). Medicare $1,045.09. After tax and Medicare = $117.11 per week. See [take-home](/topics/take-home) page for more.

### How does the average American salary compare?

While the average American salary is often quoted in US dollars, Australian pay rates are set by Fair Work Commission. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings: full-time adult ordinary time $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That’s $108,352.40 annual. That’s higher than the National Minimum Wage. But the average American salary is a common reference point. Our calculator uses Australian rates.

## Using the timesheet calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you type your base hourly rate. Check the box for casual loading. The calculator shows annual gross, super on top. It’s an estimate. Not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

Converting hourly to annual: hourly × hours per week × 52. Assume 38 hours. Super paid on top. Casual loading 25% on top. Tax and Medicare. See [reference tables](/data) for more data.
